steps.prompt: Your class wants a longer recess. What would the principal say against it?

cards.title: Give the other side
cards.body: A counterclaim is what someone who disagrees would say: “Some people argue that…”, “Critics say…”, “It is true that…”. Including it shows you’ve thought about both sides.

cards.title: Then answer it
cards.body: A rebuttal answers the counterclaim: “However, …”, “Even so, …”, “In fact, …”. Back it up with evidence and explain it, just like a reason. Never leave a counterclaim unanswered.

cards.title: A counterclaim paragraph
cards.text: Some people argue that a school garden costs too much. However, seeds and tools cost less than one class trip, and local stores often donate supplies. This shows that a garden is one of the cheapest ways to improve our school.
cards.note: Counterclaim → rebuttal with a fact → explanation.

prompts: Was your counterclaim fair to the other side?
What evidence made your rebuttal convincing?
